exposure: power dynamics between patient and provider
outcome: women's ability to participate in decision-making
women's ability to make health care decisions for themselves and their children
cohort: The study recruited 22 self-identified women of color, aged 18 or older, who were between six weeks and one year postpartum.
finding: Providers' control over information shared with women of color during pregnancy and birth created a power dynamic that diminished women's autonomy and ability to make health care decisions.
cross-section timing: Interviews were conducted when participants were between six weeks and one year postpartum, exploring their experiences during pregnancy and birth.
